target.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nothing limits how often recurring cron jobs can fire. An agent (or CLI caller) can schedule a `30s` job that runs an LLM turn forever — on hosted/operator deployments that is unbounded spend with no operator control. Cron has a concurrency guardrail (`cron.maxConcurrentRuns`) but no cadence guardrail. Related: #76473 explores a warning-only variant; this PR is the enforceable operator limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

One opt-in config value, `cron.minInterval`, enforced in two layers:

1. **Creation/edit rejection (UX layer):** `create`, schedule-changing `update`, and declaration-keyed `add` converges of a recurring `every`/`cron` job below the floor fail with a clear error (`cron schedule fires every 30s, below the minimum interval of 5m`; gateway maps it to `INVALID_REQUEST`). The cron tool description tells agents to increase the interval instead of retrying. For `cron` expressions this samples upcoming fires — documented as best-effort, since bounded sampling cannot prove an expression's true minimum gap.
2. **Fire-time floor (enforcement layer):** the scheduler paces every `nextRunAtMs` re-arm so consecutive fires of a recurring job stay at least `minInterval` apart (start-to-start, launchd `ThrottleInterval`-style). This is the contract the docs promise: it covers jobs created before the limit was configured, expressions whose tight gaps escape sampling, restarts/missed-slot catch-up, error-backoff retries, update re-arms, and maintenance recomputes. Deferred fires log a warning naming the job.

Scope decisions: one-shot `at` jobs are exempt; forced manual runs never shift the schedule and are not floored; transient-failure retries still follow `cron.retry` but recurring re-fires are lower-bounded by the floor; a 2s dispatch slack (clamped to half the floor) keeps schedules whose cadence exactly equals the floor on their natural slots — no drift, no warning spam.

## User Impact

None by default: unset/`0` means no limit and preserves shipped behavior exactly. With the limit set:

```json5
{
  cron: {
    minInterval: "5m", // duration string ("30s", "5m", "1h") or milliseconds
  },
}
```

recurring jobs neither validate nor fire more often than every 5 minutes. Config surface: `CronConfig.minInterval` + zod schema with duration validation, help text, label, and docs (`docs/automation/cron-jobs.md`, `docs/cli/cron.md`, configuration reference).

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. The rebase re-ported validation and the floor onto main's refactored update path (`updateLoadedJob`/`finalizeUpdatedJob`), and extended creation-time validation to the declarative `add()` converge path — post-refactor, an `add` with a `declarationKey` could otherwise change an existing job's schedule without hitting the floor check.

- Post-rebase, all green (4 Vitest shards): full cron subsystem (`src/cron`, 100+ test files), `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`, `src/config/cron-limits.test.ts`, `src/config/zod-schema.cron-min-interval.test.ts`, `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts`, `test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts`.
- Behavior tests (`src/cron/service.min-interval-floor.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/jobs.min-interval.test.ts`, extended `timer.regression`): pre-existing every/cron jobs paced + warned; error-path pacing; no-floor regression guard; at-floor cadence stays on natural slots under dispatch jitter; force runs preserve the schedule; enable-toggle update keeps the floor; startup catch-up does not replay a missed slot inside the floor window.
- `tsgo` core/test lanes clean for touched code; prompt snapshots regenerated via `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`.
- Multi-agent adversarial review of the floor ran pre-push; every confirmed finding (force-run schedule shift, enable-toggle bypass, restart catch-up/backoff bypasses, at-floor jitter drift, maintenance repair undoing deferrals) is fixed and regression-tested above.
